description: When the hate online is loud and the accusations are flying, David shows us what to do. Not clapbacks. Not receipts. Integrity and honesty.
excerpt: He does not fight back with words. He does not try to prove them wrong. He turns his face toward God and asks Him to handle it.
verse: "See how many enemies I have and how viciously they hate me! Protect me! Rescue my life from them! Do not let me be disgraced, for in you I take refuge. May integrity and honesty protect me, for I put my hope in you."
body_html:
I wonder if this was a hard social media day when I highlighted these verses.

Being the Co-CEO of GiveSendGo, there are days when the hate online is loud. Really loud. Vicious in the way David describes here. Coming from every direction. Saying things that aren't true. Attacking my character. Attacking the mission. Attacking me personally.

Days when it feels like everyone hates me.

They can be brutal.

And I wonder if that is why I highlighted these verses. Because David felt it too. Not the online part. But the vicious hatred part. He knew what it was like to look around and feel outnumbered by people who wanted him gone.

But watch how quickly he shifts.

He names the reality. See how many enemies I've. He doesn't pretend it isn't there. He doesn't put on a brave face and act like it doesn't sting.

Then he goes straight to God.

Protect me. Rescue my life from them. Do not let me be disgraced.

He doesn't fight back with words or go on the counter attack. He doesn't try to prove them wrong. He turns his face toward God and asks Him to handle it.

And then he says something I think is beautiful.

May integrity and honesty protect me.

Not clapbacks. Not receipts. Not sharper arguments. Integrity and honesty.

He is saying God, if I just keep walking with You, if I just keep doing what is right, that itself will be my protection. Because a life of integrity doesn't need to defend itself the way a life without it does. The truth stands on its own over time. The character speaks louder than the accusations. God is the one who vindicates.

That is such a good reminder for anyone who has ever felt piled on.

You don't have to answer every voice, correct every lie, or prove yourself to every person who wants to see you fail. You just have to keep walking with God, keep being who you are, keep letting integrity and honesty be your posture.

And let Him handle the rest.

I want the hard days to actually mean something.

Because if I let it, criticism can grow me. Attacks can teach me things. Hard seasons can carve away the parts of me that weren't really from God to begin with.

That doesn't mean I've to enjoy the hate. It just means I don't have to waste it.

And no matter what anyone says about me on any given day, God is still working. He is still shaping me. He is still finishing what He started in me. And the noise of the internet doesn't get to interrupt that.

I don't want to be distracted. Not by the loudest or meanest voices, not by how many people dislike me on a given day, not by the accusations or the drama.

That is who I'm running to when the arrows are flying.
question: Where in your life are the loudest voices distracting you from the work God is doing in you?
